method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading, formula-by-formula comparison and reverse paraphrase; not independent or human review.
scope: All twelve translated content blocks in the integers section, including proof steps, the quotient definition, representative notation, operation/order definitions, footnote, commented proof material and exercise.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Every integer can be represented by a difference of naturals and that data by an ordered pair, but pairs themselves cannot be identified with integers because equal differences such as 0−2 and 4−6 come from unequal pairs.
samples.checks: The motivating representation, the deliberately naive proposal, its counterexample and the rejection of Nat-squared as the integer set all remain explicit.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Pairs (a,b) and (c,d) are equivalent exactly when a+d=c+b. Reflexivity uses commutativity; symmetry reverses the equality; transitivity combines the two assumed equalities and cancels the common terms to obtain a+n=m+b.
samples.checks: The iff condition, proposition and every displayed or inline equality in the three-part proof are unchanged; property labels remain distinct.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Integers are the equivalence classes of pairs of naturals under Intequiv. The text then postpones possible philosophical reactions to this stipulative definition while developing technical details.
samples.checks: The quotient expression Int=Nat²/Intequiv and the philosophical-versus-technical transition are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The class containing (m,n) gets a readable representative notation. Addition, multiplication and order on classes are defined by the exact displayed representatives and cross-sum inequality, with full well-definedness checks deferred to the cited section.
samples.checks: Representative notation, element token, footnote reference, set-builder condition, all three operation/order definitions and the check-section reference have exact structural parity.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Because the constructed naturals are not literally the constructed integers, n is embedded as the class [n,0]. The embedding must preserve addition, multiplication and order; multiplication is derived line by line, and the other two conditions are assigned as an exercise.
samples.checks: All three compatibility laws, four multiplication derivation lines, commented proof material, reference and exercise are retained without changing mathematical symbols.
